capabilities: Render rough notation as math in Live Preview and Reading view without changing the note text
Bake selections, lines or whole notes into inline or display LaTeX via commands
Replace arrow and sign shortcuts (->, <=, [deg]) carried over from Symbols Prettifier
Edit text shortcuts and custom regex formula rules in the settings tab
Protect code, frontmatter, links, tables and existing math from conversion
disambiguation: Not a Markdown formatter or linter; it only converts rough math notation into rendered MathJax and LaTeX.
extras: Manual install by copying files into the plugins folder; release assets are built and attested by GitHub Actions; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author built it for real optometry notes that mix prose, formulas and machine identifiers, so formulas get typeset while everything else is left alone.
problem: Obsidian's math rendering requires correctly written LaTeX, so quickly typed rough notation like L^' = L + F or sqrt r^2-y^2 stays plain text.
summary: Rule-based converter that renders rough math notation such as n^(-1) as MathJax while typing, in Reading view, or baked into LaTeX.
